messages.author: 25a4f5811cd7d59e
messages.subject: Re: RApache installation
parts:
On Fri, Jul 13, 2012 at 3:32 PM, EricSonghill <sebasti...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hi,
> I installed RApache on a fresh XUbuntu 64 Bit by doing the following steps:
>
> STEP #0:
> Installed XUbuntu 12.04 64 Bit
>
> STEP #1:
> Installed all the updates.
>
> STEP #2:
> Installed R using $ sudo apt-get install r-base
> This Installs R version 2.14.1 (2011-12-22).
>
> STEP #3: Installed MySQL related stuff using
> sudo apt-get install mysql-common mysql-source-5.5 mysql-server-5.5
> libmysqld-dev libmysqlclient-dev mysql-client
> Installed the RMySQL package as well ( it's import to install packages using
> install.package("package.name", lib = "/usr/lib/R/library" ) so that all
> users can have access to the package.
>
> STEP #4:
> Install Apache Web Server:
> sudo apt-get install apache2
> sudo apt-get install apache2-mpm-prefork apache2-prefork-dev
> sudo apt-get install libapreq2
> nmap 127.0.0.1 to make sure that the Apache Web Server is running.
>
> STEP #5:
> Download and build rApache.
> cd /opt/
> sudo mkdir rApache
> cd rApache
> sudo wget http://rapache.net/rapache-1.1.21.tar.gz
> sudo tar -zxvf rapache-1.1.21.tar.gz
> sudo ./configure
> sudo make
>
>
> STEP #6:
> sudo vim /etc/ld.so.conf
> Add one line : /usr/lib/R/lib
>
>
> STEP #7:
> sudo vim /etc/apache2/apache2.conf
> Added the following:
> LoadModule R_module /usr/lib/apache2/modules/mod_R.so
> <Location /RApacheInfo>
> SetHandler r-info
> </Location>
>
>
> STEP #8:
> Install the brew package
> sudo R
> install.packages( ls"brew", lib = "usr/lib/R/lib" )
>
>
> STEP #9:
> Restart Ubuntu.
> Open FireFox.
> Browse to 127.0.0.1.
> Make sure that Apache is working.
> Go to 127.0.0.1/RApacheInfo
> rApache should be working.
>
> STEP #10:
> sudo mkdir /var/www/brew
> Add this to /etc/apache2/appache2.conf:
> <Directory /var/www/brew>
> SetHandler r-script
> RHandler brew::brew
> </Directory>
>
> STEP #11:
> sudo mkdir /var/www/images
> chmod 7777 /var/www/images
> Purpose of this folder is to store R plots.
>
>
>
> This actually work very well but I have a few issues and questions:
> #1 Is there any way to avoid STEP #11 ?? If not, is STEP #11 a security
> concern ?

You don't need to make it writeable to the world. www-data is probably
the user that runs the apache web server (at least it is on Ubuntu
10.04) so you should be able to
chmod it to 0755 and chown it to www-data:www-data.

> #2 Is it good to install Apache the way I did or do I have to create a
> separate user account for "Apache" ?

Perfectly fine to install apache that way. No you don't need a separate user

> #3 Same question for MySQL ...should I create a separate user account for
> MySQL ?

That's beyond the scope of this user group.

> #4 Same question for rApache ......

No.

> #5 if I go to http://127.0.0.1/brew/ the download dialog shows up ? ( and
> says that
> "you have chosen to open [space] which is a httpd/unix-directory ( 0 byes )
> from http://127.0.0.1 " ...
> How can I get rid of this ?

You could set the Options +index on that directory to list the contents:

http://httpd.apache.org/docs/2.2/mod/core.html#options


> #6 Any other advice / hints on how to make this installation more secure ?

Looks good so far ;)

jeff

messages.author: 3ea57457192f4f3b
messages.subject: Re: RApache installation
parts:
On Fri, Jul 13, 2012 at 10:32 PM, EricSonghill
<sebasti...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> STEP #11:
> sudo mkdir /var/www/images
> chmod 7777 /var/www/images
> Purpose of this folder is to store R plots.

That looks like poor design, who gave you this idea? :-) Better is to
store images outside of /var/www/ with a unique identifier and have an
R script that sends those images dynamically. E.g if your application
generates a PNG file, you could store it in /tmp with some random uuid
as filename. E.g. /tmp/a7e9c290-cd2e-11e1-9b23-0800200c9a66.

Then you pass on the uuid to the client through ajax or so, and you
expose an R script through rapache that can be used to retrieve the
images. Something like this:

## begin getimages.R

uuid <- GET$uuid;
filename <- file.path("/tmp", uuid);
stopifnot(file.exists(filename))

setContentType(type='image/png')
sendBin(object=readBin(filename,'raw',n=file.info(filename)$size))

## end R script

The client can than go to .e.g
http://something.com/R-files/getimages.R?uuid=a7e9c290-cd2e-11e1-9b23-0800200c9a66
and will get the image.

messages.subject: Re: RApache installation
parts: I updated/added two lines to Step 5:

STEP #5:
Download and build rApache.
cd /opt/
sudo mkdir rApache
cd rApache

sudo wget http://rapache.net/rapache-1.2.0.tar.gz
sudo tar -zxvf rapache-1.2.0.tar.gz
   cd ./rapache-1.2.0 
sudo ./configure
sudo make
   sudo make install

STEP #6:
sudo vim /etc/ld.so.conf
Add one line :  /usr/lib/R/lib


STEP #7:
sudo vim /etc/apache2/apache2.conf
Added the following:
LoadModule R_module /usr/lib/apache2/modules/mod_R.so
<Location /RApacheInfo>
SetHandler r-info
</Location>

But I get a similar error to others--When I try to start Apache2, it says it can't load the R_Module:

$ sudo service apache2 start
   * Starting web server apache2
     apache2: Syntax error on line 240 of /etc/apache2/apache2.conf: Can't locate API module structure `R_Module' in file /usr/lib/apache2/modules/mod_R.so: /usr/lib/apache2/modules/mod_R.so: undefined symbol: R_Module
    Action 'start' failed.
    The Apache error log may have more information.
     ...fail!

Anyone know what I am doing wrong? How to fix?

messages.author: 4dd9d775fef6ed8d
messages.subject: Re: RApache installation
parts:
I finally figured out what I did wrong in Step 7 --- a simple typo -- I can't believe it !

upper case on the 2nd "M"  -- wrong:
LoadModule R_Module /usr/lib/apache2/modules/mod_R.so
should be: 
LoadModule R_module /usr/lib/apache2/modules/mod_R.so

Also I re-did the configure in Step 5 using this (from http://rapache.net/manual.html) and it helped:
./configure \
    --with-R=/usr/bin/R \
    --with-apache2-apxs=/usr/bin/apxs2 \
Also here are some more typos in the steps that I fixed:
